subgroups.name: solve 1

steps.hints: ❓ Did you change where the dialog frame is set in the code?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ Where in the code should the dialog frame be set, so that the directions appear in the correct frame?


Solution: 

setDialogFrame code should be cut and pasted in line 3, above showLongText.
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, the directions appear in the default dialog frame, instead of the one selected in the code.


Fix the bugs in the code so that the directions appear in the correct frame.

subgroups.introduction: Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!

validationItems.text: setDialogFrame code moved to line 3, above showLongText.

subgroups.name: solve 2

steps.hints: ❓ Does the code in the event argument in each controller.A event match the corresponding comments and images?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ Which button image should show when the A button is pressed? 

❓ Which button image should show when the A button is released?


Solution: 

The event argument should be changed to ControllerButtonEvent.Pressed on line 70 and changed to ControllerButtonEvent.Released on line 108.
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, the wrong image appears!


Fix the bugs in the code so that when the A button is pressed the image appears pushed in and when the A button is released the image is reset.

subgroups.name: solve 3

steps.hints: ❓ Did you move the changeScoreBy function inside the code that runs when the A button is pressed?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ How can you cut and paste text to place code on a different line in the editor?

❓ Where should the changeScoreBy function be placed so that the score changes by 1, each time the A button is pressed?


Solution: 

The changeScoreBy function should be cut and pasted inside the curly brackets of controller.A.onEvent(ControllerButtonEvent.Pressed)
steps.instructions:
When you click ▶, the score is changed only once.


Fix the bugs in the code so that the score changes by 1, each time the A button is pressed.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 3 of Blue Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about block statements. In JavaScript, instead of adding code into different containers, you’ll add block statements inside curly brackets { } of an event or a loop. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 3:

badges.title: Thinking Inside the Block
badges.description: Use block statements inside curly brackets { } to add code inside of events and loops.

badges.title: Projectile Manager
badges.description: Create a  projectile in JavaScript.

badges.title: Game On (Update Interval)
badges.description: Use a game update loop in JavaScript.

badges.title: About Yay High
badges.description: Use the screen object’s height property instead of a number.

badges.title: Framing the Discussion
badges.description: Use setDialogFrame to design a custom text box.

badges.title: Settle the Score
badges.description: Set the score in JavaScript.

badges.title: Cute as a Button
badges.description: Use a button event in JavaScript.
